Ravi Kumar --Applicant
 Versus
State Of Uttarakhand --Respondent
Hon'ble Siddhartha Sah, J.
Mr. Gaurav Singh, learned counsel for the
applicant appeared through V.C.
2. Mr. Tumul Nainwal, learned A.G.A. for the
State.
3. By means of the present Anticipatory Bail
Application, the applicant is seeking anticipatory
bail in FIR dated 22.04.2026, registered as FIR
No.0364 of 2026, under Section 308(5) of BNS,
2023, Police Station Laksar, District Haridwar.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant would
submit that the FIR has been lodged by the
informant alleging therein that on 19.04.2026 at
about 19:07 hours a call from unknown
telephone number was received on his mobile
phone threatening him to give Rs.10,00,000/-
otherwise he would be shot dead and some
unknown persons were also chasing him. The FIR
was registered as FIR No.0364 of 2026 under
Section 308 (5) of BNS, 2023 at Police Station
Laksar, District Haridwar.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant would
submit that the alleged mobile phone used in

extortion does not belong to the present
applicant.
6. He would further submit that the only
evidence against the present applicant is the
statement of the co-accused in the police custody.
Apart from this, there is no evidence on record
which links the present applicant with the alleged
offence.
7. He would further submit that to make out a
case under Section 308 (5) of BNS, it is necessary
that there must be actual delivery of the amount
extorted and in absence of such delivery, mere
demand is not sufficient to invoke the said
offence.
8. Per contra, learned State counsel would
submit that from the report itself, it is ex-facie
clear that the applicant-accused had made the
demand call from his phone and which is one of
the reasons for rejection of the anticipatory bail
application by the Additional District & Sessions
Judge, Laksar, District Haridwar.
9. He would further submit that the applicant
has criminal antecedents of three criminal cases
against him. He would further submit that
looking to the seriousness of the offence and the
criminal antecedents, the applicant does not
deserve anticipatory bail.
10. On this, learned counsel for the applicant
would submit that, in fact, there are only two
cases against the applicant and that too of Drug
and Cosmetic Act and Mines and Minerals Act.
11. He would further rely upon a judgment of
the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Salib @

Shalu @ Salim vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and
others, reported in (2023) 20 Supreme Court
cases 194 and has drawn the attention of the
Court to para 24 thereof, which is being extracted
hereunder for ready reference:-
"24. Thus, it is relevant to note that nowhere the first
informant has stated that out of fear, she paid Rs 10 lakhs
to the accused persons. To put it in other words, there is
nothing to indicate that there was actual delivery of
possession of property (money) by the person put in fear.
In the absence of anything to even remotely suggest that
the first informant parted with a particular amount after
being put to fear of any injury, no offence under Section
386 IPC can be said to have been made out."
12. Placing reliance upon para 24, he would
submit that to make out a case under Section
386 of IPC, there has to be actual delivery of
possession of property (money) by the person put
in fear.
13. He would further submit that from a bare
reading of the FIR, it is abundantly clear that
there has been no delivery of money in the
present case and thus the offence under Section
308(5) of BNS would not be made out in the
present case.
14. After having heard the learned counsel for
the parties and after going through the record, it
is evident from the bare reading of the FIR that
there is a mere allegation of extortion demand
against the applicant and there is no delivery of
any money.
15. It is also clear from the submissions of
learned counsel for the applicant that there is no
previous criminal history of similar nature.
16. Having considered the submissions

advanced by learned counsel for the parties, but
without expressing any opinion on the final
merits of the case, this Court is of the view that
the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on
anticipatory bail. Accordingly, the anticipatory
bail application deserves to be allowed.
17. The Anticipatory Bail Application is allowed.
18. In the eventuality of arrest, the applicant
shall be enlarged on bail on his furnishing a
personal bond in the sum of Rs.20,000/- with
two sureties, each in the like amount, to the
satisfaction of the Investigating Officer ("IO"). In
addition to it, the applicant shall also comply with
the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall co-operate with the
investigation.
(ii) The applicant shall not approach any
witness/victim in any manner, whatsoever.
(iii)The applicant shall not leave the country
without prior permission of the concerned
court.
(iv) The applicant shall deposit his passport
with the Investigating Officer ("IO"). The
passport may only be returned by the order of
the court concerned. In case the applicant does
not have passport, he shall give an undertaking
to that effect to the IO.
(v) The applicant shall also give an undertaking
on (i), (ii) & (iii) above.
(Siddhartha Sah, J.)
